How to use this guide

Read one lesson, complete the action in your business, and keep the result somewhere you can find it. The examples are illustrations, not claims about real customers.

LESSON 01 / 10

Define one offer customers can actually purchase

Broad menus make it hard to communicate value and understand margins.

What to do

  1. Write your core service or product in everyday language.
  2. Clarify inclusions, exclusions, delivery time, pricing approach and next action.
  3. Design the simplest offer package you can genuinely deliver.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: one clear service tier with an honest starting price and an easy booking route.

AVOID THIS

Bundling ten services before understanding demand.

↗
What you should finish with

One-page offer sheet.

Evidence to capture: A working offer and delivery commitment
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a one-page offer sheet with verified features, scope, exclusions, price and a customer-facing CTA.
LESSON 02 / 10

Calculate true unit economics

An attractive price can still lose money on every sale.

What to do

  1. List revenue per transaction and genuinely variable expenses.
  2. Calculate contribution after variable costs; identify fixed monthly overhead.
  3. Model break-even volume and the capacity required to serve it.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: price minus therapist commission, materials and transaction fees yields contribution.

AVOID THIS

Treating gross revenue as profit or forgetting payment fees.

↗
What you should finish with

Unit-economics calculator inputs and break-even statement.

Evidence to capture: Inputs for price, variable costs and fixed costs
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a contribution-margin and break-even worksheet using my supplied numbers and no fabricated inputs.
LESSON 03 / 10

Build a survival budget

Profitable businesses can still fail through cash timing.

What to do

  1. Record one-off launch costs, deposits, inventory, platform charges and monthly commitments.
  2. Forecast actual expected cash collections and payments by week.
  3. Show a downside case and the minimum money required to continue safely.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: deposits for equipment may be due months before launch receipts arrive.

AVOID THIS

Assuming every invoice will be collected immediately.

↗
What you should finish with

13-week cash forecast with assumptions.

Evidence to capture: Cost quotes and payment schedules
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a 13-week cash forecast with real payment timing, opening cash, receipts, expenses and runway.
LESSON 04 / 10

Design the service delivery loop

Customer experience breaks when the underlying work is undefined.

What to do

  1. Map enquiry → quote → payment → fulfillment → follow-up.
  2. Identify each owner, handoff, supplier, tool and failure point.
  3. Set one quality standard and one fallback procedure.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: booking request → availability check → invoice → assignment → completion → feedback.

AVOID THIS

Building automation before defining the manual process.

↗
What you should finish with

Service blueprint and first SOP.

Evidence to capture: One real fulfillment or dry-run record
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Write an operational SOP for one transaction with owner, handoffs, exceptions and quality check.
LESSON 05 / 10

Create the brand minimum

Branding should clarify the offer, not delay customer learning.

What to do

  1. Write a clear business name, promise, audience, tone and visual direction.
  2. Prepare authentic photos and logo assets; use temporary placeholders where needed.
  3. Check contact consistency across the site, emails and social profiles.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: one name, dark neutral palette, authentic service photos and consistent booking CTA.

AVOID THIS

Over-investing in a logo while buyers cannot understand the offer.

↗
What you should finish with

Compact brand kit and verified asset list.

Evidence to capture: A brand brief with real contact details
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Build a practical brand brief with name, positioning, voice, palette, photography needs and CTA.
LESSON 06 / 10

Design the first conversion experience

A clear page can validate interest without a complete app.

What to do

  1. Sketch or prototype using a tool such as Lovable if it helps you visualize quickly.
  2. Create one useful landing page with offer, credibility, FAQs and a clear contact action.
  3. Confirm the page works on mobile and tracks meaningful enquiries.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: a lightweight landing page plus WhatsApp enquiry; no unnecessary login or features.

AVOID THIS

Mistaking an attractive prototype for a verified business.

↗
What you should finish with

Mobile-first landing-page brief and test page.

Evidence to capture: A working preview and successful test enquiry
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Prepare a simple landing-page specification with mobile layout, copy, assets, CTA and enquiry measurement.
LESSON 07 / 10

Own the essentials of your digital identity

Customers should find and contact the same business wherever they land.

What to do

  1. Check available business name/domain and select a sensible domain.
  2. Set up reliable email and verified contact methods.
  3. Reserve relevant social handles, complete platform profiles and link back to the main offer.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: a custom domain, matching email signature, complete Facebook and Instagram bios.

AVOID THIS

Buying every possible domain or creating accounts you cannot maintain.

↗
What you should finish with

Digital asset and account inventory.

Evidence to capture: Working domain/email/profile links
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a domain, email and social-profile setup checklist for this business and track ownership and access.
LESSON 08 / 10

Choose Google visibility only where eligible

Local visibility helps qualified businesses but an inaccurate listing risks problems.

What to do

  1. Check Google Business Profile eligibility before setup.
  2. If eligible, choose legitimate storefront or service-area configuration and actual business details.
  3. If not eligible, use your website, SEO and appropriate alternative channels instead.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: a mobile service may qualify as service-area business; an online-only brand usually does not.

AVOID THIS

Using fake addresses, virtual offices or invented reviews.

↗
What you should finish with

Local discovery plan, including a justified GBP decision.

Evidence to capture: Eligibility decision and source link
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a GBP eligibility screening script and an alternative discovery plan if I am not eligible.
LESSON 09 / 10

Run a measured first-market test

Launch activity should produce learning, not just reach.

What to do

  1. Choose one buyer segment and one offer.
  2. Test a small set of Meta ads, direct outreach or partner referrals as appropriate.
  3. Record leads, conversion, acquisition costs where known, objections and service delivery feedback.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: test two honest ad messages against the same offer with a strict spend ceiling.

AVOID THIS

Scaling ads based on likes before confirming leads and contribution margin.

↗
What you should finish with

First 14-day marketing test and review sheet.

Evidence to capture: Actual campaign or outreach outcomes
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Design a 14-day marketing experiment with campaign brief, small spend cap, lead tracking and a clear continue/stop rule.
LESSON 10 / 10

Build a usable 90-day operating plan

A plan only matters when someone owns the next action.

What to do

  1. Choose milestones across validation, setup, sales, delivery and reporting.
  2. Assign owners, dates, resources and completion checks.
  3. Review weekly; change the plan based on evidence, not arbitrary calendar pressure.
EXAMPLE / ILLUSTRATIVE

Illustrative: weeks 1–2 customer test; 3–4 offer adjustments; 5–8 launch channels; 9–13 process review.

AVOID THIS

Treating arbitrary projections as commitments or omitting dependencies.

↗
What you should finish with

90-day milestones and weekly review rhythm.

Evidence to capture: Documented priorities and weekly reporting owner
Optional: copy a ChatGPT prompt ＋

The lesson does not need AI. This prompt is only a writing aid.

Create a 90-day execution plan with a weekly calendar, owners, dependencies, milestone definitions and risk triggers.
